title: reduce streaming token latency: token loop, flush cadence, backpressure, kernel scheduling, KV cache
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation:
Reducing token emission latency for streaming responses is a high-priority production objective (see ENG-2981, ENG-3050). Customers observed tail-latency spikes when the token loop flush cadence and backpressure interaction caused batching fragmentation and kernel scheduling stalls on busy nodes. This PR implements a coordinated set of runtime improvements to reduce median and tail streaming latency while preserving throughput and stability.

Summary of changes:
- Token loop: convert blocking flush path to an async-aware non-blocking flush that yields to the scheduler when backpressure is detected. This reduces artificial head-of-line stalls when a single slow client holds socket buffer space.
- Flush cadence: introduce adaptive flush cadence that tracks per-connection write buffer pressure and model generation rate; default cadence is unchanged but the controller will advance flushes early under high backpressure to avoid large micro-bursts.
- Backpressure handling: add a per-request backpressure score exposed to the scheduler; requests with severe backpressure can be gently deprioritized to reduce tail token latency for other streams.
- Kernel scheduling: implement lightweight preemptive scheduling hooks in serve/scheduler/preemptive_scheduler.cpp to prioritize streaming token emission kernels over long-running batched kernels when p95 latency targets are at risk. The scheduler uses cheap heuristics (kv cache hit ratio, sequence length, backpressure) to pick preemption candidates.
- KV cache: optimize hot-key lookups and alignment to avoid cache thrashing across concurrent streams. Improve batch-friendly access patterns in serve/kv_cache/kv_cache.cpp to increase effective hit ratio under continuous batching.
- Continuous batching: better alignment of small streaming requests into short-lived micro-batches without increasing blocking; update continuous_batcher to favor latency-bound flows.
- Observability: add metrics streaming.flush_count, streaming.flush_latency_ms, scheduling.preemptions, kv_cache.hit_ratio and expose to Console dashboards. Docs added under docs/observability.

Commits (high-level):
- a1b2c3: token loop non-blocking flush and API changes
- d4e5f6: adaptive flush controller and config flags
- f7g8h9: preemptive scheduler prototype and unit tests
- i0j1k2: KV cache hot-key alignment and micro-benchmarks
- l3m4n5: continuous batcher tuning + integration tests
- o6p7q8: metrics + docs + bench harness updates

Files/areas changed (high level):
- serve/streaming: token_loop, flush_controller and tests
- serve/scheduler: new preemptive scheduler and tests
- serve/kv_cache: access pattern optimizations
- serve/batching: continuous batcher heuristics
- serve/metrics & docs: new metrics and observability docs
- tests/benchmarks: synthetic and replay-based latency benchmarks

Performance results (benchmarked on c5d-dedicated cluster):
- Short sequences (<=32 tokens): median token latency down ~35%, p95 down ~28%
- Medium sequences (32-128 tokens): median down ~20%, p95 down ~25%
- Long sequences (>128 tokens): median down ~15%, p95 down ~18%
- End-to-end throughput unchanged (+/-2%); kernel utilization slightly improved.
Bench harness: benchmarks/streaming/latency_p95.yaml. Repro script included.

Testing:
- Unit tests added for flush controller and preemptive scheduler.
- Integration tests under tests/streaming simulate mixed load and validate no regression in throughput and correctness.
- Stress/poke-run: ran 6h canary on dedicated cluster with no crashes, no memory leaks.

CI notes:
- Initial CI run failed due to a flaky kernel unit test (race in preemptive scheduling test). Fixed with a lightweight barrier in tests; CI green on rerun. All checks (build, unit, integration, lint) passed prior to merge.

Rollback and rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime.feature.streaming_low_latency (off by default).
- Canaries: release to 1% of Dedicated pools, monitor streaming.flush_latency_ms and scheduling.preemptions for 24-48h.
- If p99 regressions observed, automatically disable via rollout policy and fallback to previous scheduler.

Notes for reviewers:
- Most logic is behind a flag and guarded; linking to ENG-2981 for risk window and canary plan.
- We kept kernel changes conservative: no ABI changes, just added light-weight scheduling hooks.

Requested reviewers: Miguel (scheduling), Jean-Luc (kv/cache), Priya (bench/metrics).
review_comments: Miguel Santos: Can you explain how preemption interacts with continuous batching? Will we fragment batches and lose throughput?

Aisha Patel (author): The preemption hook is designed to run only when backpressure score exceeds threshold and only preempts at micro-batch boundaries; we added a heuristic to avoid preempting large throughput batches. See serve/scheduler/preemptive_scheduler.cpp lines 120-185. Throughput regression is within noise (+/-2%).
Jean-Luc Moreau: Please add a metric for kv_cache evictions so we can monitor thrash during canary.
Aisha Patel (author): Added kv_cache.eviction_count and kv_cache.hit_ratio; updated docs and dashboards.
Priya Kumar: Tests look good; CI flake observed in test_preemption, please ensure barrier is robust across platforms.
Aisha Patel (author): Added explicit test barrier using TestSync primitive; re-ran CI and tests are stable.
release_notes: Reduced streaming token emission latency by improving token loop flush cadence, introducing adaptive backpressure handling, adding lightweight preemptive kernel scheduling, and optimizing KV cache access patterns. Flagged behind runtime.feature.streaming_low_latency; expected median token latency reductions of 15-35% depending on sequence length. Added observability metrics for monitoring.
